_about: Wolves at night (scripts/wolves.gd; Alex, 2026-11-16, docs/DIRECTION.md: renting space in Lars's barn keeps her animals safe from wolves). Once a night, at `hour`, there is a `chance` that wolves come for her pens, but only once Act 1 is done and only if some animal is at risk (wolves.at_risk()). At risk means: her sheep that aren't in their barn stalls (`housed`, flock bedtime), and the penned wild animals beyond the `barn_stalls` (data/wildlife.json) that Lars's barn shelters while its rent is paid up (wildlife.stalls_rented()). The rented stalls shelter the wild animals first, then any sheep out in the pen. When they come she hears a howl and a toast, and `min_pack` to `max_pack` wolves of the sizes below walk in from the woods `spawn_dist` metres off towards the pen. She has `window` real seconds (not counting the title, a story scene, the cinematic camera or a pause) to see them off: Nora running at one inside `shy` metres, or the dog's bark while she plays him inside `bark_range`, takes one of its `nerve` (one at most every `hit_every` seconds each); a wolf with none left runs back into the woods. Miss the window and they take one animal at risk; a morning note says which. If she sleeps through the night (bed before `hour`), the night is rolled in the morning at `asleep_chance` and a hit takes one animal while she slept. `walk` and `run` are metres a second; `scale` is the model's size (the stand-in coyote is scaled up until the wolf models land), `stride` the ground each loop covers per second at speed 1 and scale 1 (the coyote's numbers). `fallback_model` is used while a size's own `model` isn't in the project. Every word the player sees is a draft until Alex approves it.
